\subsubsection{As the Transimpedance Amplifier (A2)}\label{sss:ampab-tia}

As A2 the amplifier holds the working electrode at $v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ on its inverting
input and converts the electrode current across the feedback resistor,
\(V_{\mathrm{OUT}} = v_{\mathrm{cm}} - I_{\mathrm{WE}} R_f\). Both current polarities
pass through $R_f$, so the ADC sees offset binary about the $v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ code.
$R_f$ is a 16-tap string spanning \SIrange{35}{560}{\kilo\ohm}.

The bench is Figure~\ref{fig:tb-tiafb}: $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, the only tap
characterised here and the only one to which the figures of this part apply, with
$C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, a \SI{5}{\pico\farad} load and the Randles electrode of
Figure~\ref{fig:randles-cell} at $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$,
$R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$. The
typical point and the Monte Carlo run are at \SI{37}{\celsius}, the four skew corners at
\SI{25}{\celsius}.
